subject: Latency window variance proposal for Hosted API (p50/p95)
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API latency commitments for renewal (p50/p95)

Karthik,

Hope you’re well. As we approach our renewal with Redwood (current term ends 2026-09-30), our product team has tightened the latency targets for our main interactive flow. We rely on Redwood Hosted for real-time scoring and need stronger p50/p95 guarantees to meet our UX SLAs.

Current ask from Nimbus: p50 <= 50ms, p95 <= 250ms (measured per region). We understand this is aggressive; before we lock the renewal we need to know if Redwood can either:
- commit these endpoints to Hosted with an exception and credits if missed, or
- propose an alternative measurement window/definition that gets us closer while reflecting production traffic.

Key context:
- Traffic is concentrated in us-west-2 (80% of requests).
- Peak concurrency per instance: ~120 requests/s; median request size typical for short prompts (~50 tokens).
- We can provide a 72-hour traffic dump and run a short pilot if helpful.

Please loop in the infra/product folks and share how you'd measure p95 (rolling 1h, daily, per-minute buckets, etc.) and any reasonable exception terms. We’d prefer a simple daily check but are flexible.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Head of Engineering | Nimbus Analytics
alex.morgan@nimbus-analytics.com
[Attachment: traffic-sample.csv (csv)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments for renewal (p50/p95)

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the context. I’ve looped in Marissa (product) and Ben (infra/runtime) to scope feasibility and a measurement definition we can operate against.

Quick summary of next steps we can take this week:
1) You share the 72-hour traffic sample (or we accept the attached subset) so infra can replay and estimate tail latency.
2) Ben to propose a measurement window and explain impact of synthetic vs. real traffic.
3) We’ll propose an exception offer (timeboxed pilot + reduced credit scale) if we can’t commit the exact numbers from day 1.

Prelim answer to your measurement question: Redwood typically measures latency SLOs using aggregated percentile over small time buckets to reduce sensitivity to short spikes. For Hosted we recommend one of these:
- Option A (tightest): p50/p95 computed on 1-minute buckets, then take the 95th percentile of those 1-minute p95 values over a rolling 30-day window (captures sustained tail).
- Option B (operationally pragmatic): p50/p95 computed from raw request latencies across a rolling 7-day window, sampled at 5s resolution, daily evaluation.

Neither is perfect for every workload — Option A is conservative for customer-facing tails, Option B is easier to explain in contracts.

I’ve attached a short measurement proposal (slo-measurement-proposal.xlsx) that outlines how credits would map to misses for both options. Can you confirm whether Nimbus prefers region-specific SLOs (us-west-2 only) or an account-wide SLO?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
[Attachment: slo-measurement-proposal.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Nimbus asks for p50 50ms / p95 250ms — what can we offer?

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Alex’s note and the traffic sample. High-level asks: p50 50ms and p95 250ms (region). Marissa, they want to know measurement and credits; Ben, I’ll need a concise explanation of what we can realistically guarantee on Hosted without moving them to Dedicated.

Questions for you both:
- Ben: can we reproduce a p95 <= 250ms on the replay in us-west-2 with current instance types? If not, what delta do you expect and what levers (quantization, batching config, KV caching) would reduce p95 vs. cost?
- Marissa: Contract side — does Redwood have precedent for region-scoped SLOs with timeboxed exception pilots and reduced credit tiers? If so, what does the wording look like (measurement window specifics + evaluation period)?

My suggested motion: propose a 60-day pilot with the following commitments:
- Measurement: Option A (1-minute bucket aggregation) but evaluated regionally for us-west-2 only.
- Interim SLO: p50 <= 70ms, p95 <= 320ms for the pilot (these are conservative but achievable)
- If pilot meets targets for 45 of 60 days, we convert to contract amendment with a staged tightening to their target over 6 months.
- Credit: sliding scale — 10% monthly credit for misses between pilot SLO and requested SLO; 25% if we miss pilot SLO by >20% for >7 days.

Ben/Marissa — any changes to the above before I send?

Thanks,
Karthik

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbus-analytics.com>, Nimbus Analytics Legal <contracts@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T17:43:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed latency window & pilot for Hosted API (p50/p95) — Nimbus renewal path

Alex — thanks for your patience while we scoped this with product and infra. Below is a concrete proposal to bridge your requested numbers with a production-safe approach.

Proposal (high level):
- Scope: Hosted API, region-scoped to us-west-2 for the pilot.
- Pilot length: 60 days (start date TBD after traffic ingest).
- Measurement definition: p50 and p95 will be calculated per 1-minute buckets (raw request latencies). For each day we compute the p50 and p95 from those 1-minute values; the pilot succeeds if the daily p95 for the region is below the pilot p95 target for at least 45 of the 60 days. We will also publish rolling 30-day aggregated percentiles for monitoring only.
- Pilot SLO targets: p50 <= 70ms, p95 <= 320ms (region-us-west-2).
- Post-pilot path: if pilot success criteria met, Redwood will work toward staged tightening to your requested p50 <= 50ms and p95 <= 250ms over a 3–6 month program, including recommended infra/config changes and optional Dedicated evaluation.
- Credits/exceptions: during the pilot we offer reduced credits (10% invoice credit for days where daily p95 is between 320–400ms; 25% if daily p95 > 400ms). After conversion to a contractual SLO we will apply standard credit language.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm you can provide the 72-hour traffic dump (we’ll sign an NDA if you prefer) and confirm a pilot start window.
2) Proposed kickoff meeting: 2026-08-24 10:00 AM PT — Ben and Marissa will join to review measurement and replay plan.
3) I’ll prepare a short contract addendum/exception letter reflecting the pilot terms for your legal team.

If this looks reasonable, I’ll circulate a calendar invite for the kickoff and attach the measurement doc and replay instructions.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
